M E S S A G E It ts a great pleasure to know that the Khasi Authors Society IS publishing a Magazine, “Ka Thiar Ki Nong- thoh " to coincide with the General Council meeting to be held in the month of September this year. As an attempt made by the Society to record the lives and achievements of tire past Khasi Authors, who have contributed toward.s the development and enrich- ment of the Khasi language and literature, this deserves high praise. Jt is undoubtedly the writings of these past authors which profoundly influenced the course of history in the Khasi literature as it is at present. I wish the Khasi Authors’ Society all success in its task of perpetuating the memory of the pioneers in the field of Khasi Leterature so that it would rekindle the spark in those, of our times with literary bent of mird, to emulate, develop and improve upon what their illustrious predecessors had achieved. I wish the Khasi Authors’ Society all success W. A. SANGMA. (Oil'ice PABX 397 Phone:) SH 6351 ( SH 68U Dr. B. PAKEM D.O. No. MI' ISTER Education and Public Relations, Dated the , 14th August, 1981 Meghalaya Shillong M E S S A G E I am really happy to note that the Khasi Authors’ Society is bringing out Volume III of “Ka Thiar Ki Nongthoh” and that the publication of the volume coincides with the Generally Council Meeting of the Society to be held in September, 19SI. It is praise- worthy on the part of the publishers to include in this particular volume the commentaries and critical appre- ciations of the works of past Khasi Authors. Such commentaries will provide the students of Khasi Lite- rature with a valuable background reference as well as re-awakened interests in the works of our great Khasi Authors, I wish the organisers every success. B. PAKEM Giams : NEHU Phone : NORTH EASTERN HILL

I congratulate the Authors’ Society on their laudable achievement and wish them greater success. The North Eastern Hill University is planning to start a Post-Graduate Department in Khasi Language and Literature in the near future, and J am sure, the scholars in this field will greatly interested in the publication as well as in the introduction of Khasi at the post-graduate level which is perhaps for the first time in the case of a tribal language within our jurisdiction. It is mh hope that when the Department is started there will be occasions for our students and teachers in this field to interact with the Authors’ Society in furthering their scholarly interests. S.
